texts.preamble: Rohan K S vs Shyamala G on 5 July, 2025 78Kabc020050982024 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Court Of Small Causes, At Bengaluru. (Scch-_25) - : Present:- Present: Sri. Raghavendra. R, B.A.L, Ll.B., Xxiii Additional Small Causes Judge, Bengaluru. Dated This The 5th Day Of July 2025 Mvc No.893/2024 Petitioner:
texts.facts: This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimant against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying to award compensation in respect of the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident occurred on 25.08.2023. 2. The case of the claimant in nutshell is that: On 25.08.2023 at about 8.45am, the petitioner was riding motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-Q-5887 from Nelamangala side towards Magadi Road via Nice Road and on reaching near Anadrahalli Bridge, the rider of the said motorcycle was made to dash against the Eicher Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AJ-4257 which was stopped and parked negligently without giving any signal. Consequently, petitioner has suffered grievous injuries. 3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to Kengannar Hospital for treatment and thereafter shifted to True Life Specialty Hospital at Nagarabhavi and admitted from 25.08.2023 to 11.09.2023 and still continuing follow up treatment. So far, he has spent Rs.8,00,000/- towards medical and nourishment expenses. Due to severe head injury the petitioner has lost his entire future in his young age. Petitioner is debarred from attending any type of works and is unable to lead normal life in rest of his life. The petitioner is suffering with permanent disability. He is not able to lead a normal life as prior to the accident. 4. It is the further case of the petitioner that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, 27 years, working as Trainee Circuit Design Engineer at Aryavarta Circuits Pvt. Ltd., and earning Rs.31,533/- per month. Due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and unable to do his profession and not getting his income. 5. The accident took place within the jurisdiction of Kamakshipalya Traffic Police under Cr.No.222/2023 against the driver of the Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AJ-4257 and rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-q-5887. Hence, the respondents being the RC Owner and the insurer of the Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AJ-4257 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, petitioner prays for award for the total compensation of Rs.35,40,000/- 6. In pursuance of notice, the respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements. 6A. The 1st respondent has filed the written statement by denying the entire petition averments except admitting the ownership of Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AJ-4257 which was insured Rohan K S vs Shyamala G on 5 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163689775/ 2 with the Respondent No.2 and the police was in force for the period from 26.07.2023 to 25.07.2024. The driver of the Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AJ- 4257 had valid driving licesne to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident. Further stated that as per the FIR it is clear that the petitioner himself is negligently driving and hit the breakdown vehicle parked on the extreme left side of the road. Further denied the injuries alleged in the accident, medical expenses, loss of amendments etc., Hence prayed for dismiss the petition against him. 6B. The 2nd respondent in its written statement has denied the entire petition averments except admitting the issuance of policy in respect of the Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AJ-4257 in favour of the 1st respondent. There is a non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act. Further stated that the driver of the Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AJ-4257 did not possess a valid and effective driving licesne as on the date of accident and the Respondent No.1 by entrusting the vehicle to a driver was not holding valid driving license knowingly. Further the respondent No.1 is using Eicher vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AJ-4257 without permit. It has denied the involvement of the vehicle in the accident and manner of accident also. Further contended that the petitioner was not wearing headgear while riding the motorcycle. Further the petitioner was was not holding valid and effective DL to ride motorcycle at the time of accident. Further contended that there is negligence on the part of the driver of the in the accident. It has denied the age, occupation, medical expenses etc., Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it. 8. In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 20 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 20. Dr.S.U.Shivaprakash got examined as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P23 to 25.
texts.arguments: Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant. The counsel for the petitioner has reliedupon the following decisions: 1. , he has opined that the petitioner has total disability at 31% and is permanent and is to the whole body. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that, 1 2011 ACJ 1 "the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The Court or Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned". 18. Our Hon'ble High Court has held in a case MFA.811 OF 2015 (MV-I) decided on 18 July, 2019 in between Rajanna @ Raju and another V/s Srinivas and another that "It is necessary to understand the meaning of the expression "permanent disability", which has been elucidated in Rajkumar. According to the Hon'ble Supreme Court, disability refers to any restriction or lack of ability to perform an activity in the manner considered normal for a human being. Permanent disability refers to the residuary incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body, found existing at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation, after achieving the maximum bodily improvement or recovery which is likely to remain for the remainder life of the injured. Temporary disability refers to the incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body on account of the injury, which will cease to exist at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation. Permanent disability can be either partial or total. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has granted future prospects to injured in a non fatal case by taking the permanent disability as 31.1% in a decision reported in 22020 SCC OnLine SC 601. The Hon'ble Apex Court has held in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, that 50% of monthly income/salary towards future prospects to be added. Therefore, Rs.26,321/- X 50%/100 future prospects Rs.13,160/-, it would meet the ends of justice. So, the monthly income of petitioner is Rs.26,321 + Rs.13160 =39,481/-. 2 Erudhaya Priya Vs State Express Transport Corporation Ltd (b) LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY: 23. The claimant has examined the Doctor to substantiate the disability as PW-3. As I have already Rohan K S vs Shyamala G on 5 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163689775/ 8 stated the notional income of the claimant is Rs.39,481/-PM, Even if any amount were to be granted under head, the petitioner will not be entitled for interest on this amount, in view of the decision in ILR 2000 Kar 1954 (Bhaskar @ Bhaskar Devaram Bangad Vs. R.K.Srinivasan & Another), wherein it is held that "the ratio in the said case would show that interest would not be payable in respect of future expenditure under different heads". NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES (GENERAL DAMAGES) (iii) Damages for pain and suffering and trauma consequence of the injuries. 24. The claimant has undergone pain and suffering during the accident and during the rehabilitation period.
